Agents swept the Awwwards Site of the Year and Site of the Month winners from 2018-2026, opened each one, and wrote down what it actually does. Then they compiled it into a skill — and tested whether the skill makes better pages. It did not, at first.

Every current figure here is generated from the dataset. Figures quoted from the project's dated decision log carry their date.

LENIS LERP 0.15 · NO DURATION KEY

01

The sweep

OFFSET-PATH THROUGH 6 STOPS · 60% TRAVEL / 40% HOLD · SCRUB 0.6 · EASE NONE

  1. Harvest131 award rowsCrawl the archives. Rows kept at 2018+, each with its award, date and live URL.
  2. Card117 sitesOne study card per site, written from the case page and the live build, then attacked by a second agent that had to disprove it.
  3. Cluster43 familiesTwo independent agents proposed taxonomies; a third reconciled them.
  4. Dissect45 deep divesPer family, a prose reference plus original re-implementations of the signature techniques.
  5. Validate2,289 → 1,118 defectsEvery constant re-checked for whether it takes effect — not just whether it was copied correctly.
  6. Compile730 constantsThe survivors became a skill an agent designs from, citing each value by record ID.

02

What broke

The interesting part is not the taxonomy. It is that the code we wrote about other people's code was the least reliable thing in the library.

1,118

defects found · 2,289 entries reviewed · nothing deleted, every one annotated where it sits

41 of 117
  1. (1)2026-08-14

    The acceptance gate checked that every citation existed, not that it was useful. Both test briefs passed while citing a priors file in which 1% of lines carried a usable constant.

    A gate that checks existence and not substance will pass a hollow artifact.

  2. (2)2026-08-14

    The first version of this page read its family's "stock easings only" as "no motion" and shipped a static document. Rejected: "no hint of awwwards at all."

    The skill now carries a motion budget per family: a strict curve set is never a small budget.

  3. (3)2026-09-24

    A hand-typed line said 32% of 2018–19 winners were offline. That was the archive-wide rate. Counted from the cards, it is 70%.

    Every current figure on this page is generated; this one was not, and it was wrong.

03

The test

Two briefs, each built by an agent with the skill and by one without it, judged blind. The skill lost both: judges preferred it 0 times in 2. After the rebuild it won 5 of 6 verdicts against the same baseline pages — one clearly, one a tie on the means. Every page below opens as built.

BARS TO SCALE /60 · SCRUB 0.6 · EASE NONE

Kiln & Quire

A two-person letterpress and risograph print studio in Kyoto that sells limited-edition prints and runs weekend workshops. Page: landing page — hero plus ONE scroll section introducing the weekend workshop. Audience: design-literate tourists and locals. The owners hate "zen minimalism" clichés.

V1 · 2026-09-23 skill 44 · base 48 won 0 of 1 judge
V2 · 2026-09-24 skill 47.7 · base 47.5 won 2 of 3 judges

Gale

An open-source time-series database built for wind-farm telemetry (millions of turbine sensor readings per second). Page: launch landing page — hero plus ONE section explaining ingest speed. Audience: infrastructure engineers. It must not look like every other dev-tool site.

V1 · 2026-09-23 skill 44 · base 46 won 0 of 1 judge
V2 · 2026-09-24 skill 51.5 · base 40.8 won 3 of 3 judges

Read with care. Two briefs, one build each; judges differ between runs, and the same baseline file scored differently (kiln-quire: 48 → 47.5; gale: 46 → 40.8). This is evidence the rebuild helped, not proof.
